dialogue.oldrepublic.archive_hoard.confi: You keep all three. Their lessons will be yours, and so will their weight. Is this your choice?
The Archive leaves your hands for good, and its knowledge goes where you send it. Is this your choice?
Unmade, the Archive is gone for everyone: no Order, no Empire and no thief will ever read it. Is this your choice?
dialogue.oldrepublic.archive_hoard.name: The Archive
dialogue.oldrepublic.archive_hoard.notes: A note in Vasch's hand is pressed into the plinth: "Whoever stands here decides what the Archive is for. I decided once. I am still counting the cost."
dialogue.oldrepublic.archive_hoard.open: Three holocrons rest in the plinth's cradles, seams faintly warm: the Watch's records under Vasch's notes, the codex from Zarvos's tomb, and his own voice. What becomes of them is yours to decide.
dialogue.oldrepublic.archive_hoard.opt.r: Scatter it back to the ruins.
Return the Archive to the Watch.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_archive_co: [An old, cold Sith voice, with Vasch's notes spoken over it:] The Zarvos Codex. Recovered from the inner vault, seal broken with the Watch key.
Zarvos wrote that every victory leaves power on the field, and the strong need only bend to pick it up. Crude. Accurate.
I took it so that no one else would. That is what I tell myself.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_archive_un: This is Orren Vasch. If you hold this, the Archive has passed out of my hands, as all things do.
I did not take it for power. I took it because a peace bought by surrender would have sold it next.
Walk lightly, reader. Everything you carry, someone else will have to carry after you.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_archive_wa: [Orren Vasch's voice, younger and careful:] Annotation, Watch Archive, shelf nine. Master Morrane's records of the plague year. Incomplete. I have restored what I could.
The Council ordered half these records destroyed so that the Empire would never read them. They would burn a library to save it. I will not.
If the Watch cannot protect what it remembers, someone must.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_common.vas: [The light stutters. Another voice cuts across the gatekeeper's, calm and close:] You keep finding my trail. Good. I am Orren Vasch, and I have waited a long time for someone who listens. Come and find me.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_jedi_kette: Knight Ruan Ketterin. I held the eastern pass for nineteen days with eleven Knights. Four of us walked out.
Then the Treaty was signed on Coruscant, and we were told the war was over. Nobody told the Empire's patrols out here.
The Watch lost its Masters, its students and half its Archive in that peace. Peace is a word. Remember the names.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_jedi_morra: Will you keep the watch with us?
I am Aveth Morrane. I founded the Watch on this frontier, when it was still a place people passed through instead of a place they fled.
We keep records because memory is a duty. Every life we failed to save is written down, so that we never fail it the same way twice.
A Jedi who forgets is only a warrior. Watch closely. See what others miss, and write it down.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_jedi_sarro: Will you carry what I learned?
Ione Sarrow. I was a healer in the old war, which means I spent it counting.
Soldiers on both sides. Settlers caught between. Children who did not know what a Republic was. The war took them all the same.
Healing is not a gentle art. It is breath forced into a body that wants to stop. Learn to breathe for others.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_jedi_vante: If you find him, will you remember what he was?
Sela Vanterre, Archivist of the Watch. I taught the young ones to read the old holocrons, and to put them back.
My best student was Orren Vasch. Patient, brilliant, gentle with every record he touched. I thought he would keep the Archive long after me.
I was wrong about what he loved. He loved the Archive more than the people it was for.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_sith_thran: Will you remember what the Empire wants?
Overseer Calix Thrane, Imperial Intelligence, frontier division. If you are hearing this, you either earned the clearance or killed someone who had it.
The Empire does not want this frontier for its soil. It wants the tombs, the crystals, and the old roads that run around the Republic's back door.
Peace is a treaty. Patience is a strategy. We are very patient.
I am Ilvane Torr, Keeper of the Sealed Dead. These tombs were not lost. We sealed them ourselves.
Some of what lies here was too dangerous even for us. The seals were meant to hold until the stars went cold.
Yet you are here, and the seals are broken. Someone came before you, with patience and a key. Find them, and ask what they took.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_sith_ysold: Ysolde. They called me the Unbowed because every one of them tried to make me kneel.
There is no law but strength. The Republic writes its laws on paper. I wrote mine on the backs of those who broke theirs.
When the lightning is spent, let it cling. Let them feel your strength long after it leaves your hands.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_sith_zarvo: Will you take what I left?
You stand in my tomb, thief or heir. I am Hadrek Zarvos, and I do not care which, so long as you are strong.
Fools think a tomb is a place of endings. A tomb is a vault. Every Lord of this frontier sealed their power in stone to wait for a worthy hand.
Power feeds on power. When your enemy falls, drink what spills.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_wayfarer_m: Will you remember where it stood?
Maelis Dunn. I drew maps for whoever paid, and for some who could not.
Maps lie by leaving things out. Mine leave out the watchtower that stood over the great sinkhole, because the Watch asked me to.
They kept something there they did not want found. When the tower fell, the ground swallowed what was left.
If you go looking, go with a light, and tell someone where you went.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_wayfarer_o: Will you remember the quiet ways?
Navigator Osk Brevan, survey scout, Republic charter. If this recording plays, my charts outlived me.
I charted this sector before the war came: every gully, every ruin, every place a ship could set down without being seen.
The first lesson of a scout is to be the quietest thing in the room. Step where the ground will not speak of you.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_wayfarer_p: Will you take the road as your teacher?
Pell, of the Long Road. No master ever took me, and none would have kept me long.
They will tell you the Force must be taught. It must be practised. Those are different things, and the road is a fine teacher if you are honest with it.
Lift what is in your way. Carry what you can. Leave the rest for the next walker.
dialogue.oldrepublic.holocron_wayfarers_: Will you carry this compass, and walk where I walked?
You found me. Good. I am Tessaly Arn, and I belonged to no Order. I walked the roads between them, where the waystones still remember who passed.
Before the war, pilgrims crossed this frontier from the Watch to the tombs and back again: Jedi, Sith, and people like me, who only wanted to understand.
The roads are lost under grass and sand now. But the Force keeps its own maps. Be still, and listen for what the ground remembers.

[In the courier's strongbox, under the poachers' pay, lies a sealed note in a fine, patient hand:] "To a reader of no Order. You found my courier, so you can find me. Come and see the Archive I have kept. O.V."
holocron.oldrepublic.archive.decided: You have already decided what becomes of the Archive.

holocron.oldrepublic.echo.jedi_morrane: Write it down, so it is not lost twice.
holocron.oldrepublic.echo.jedi_sarrow: Breathe. Then breathe for someone else.
holocron.oldrepublic.echo.jedi_vanterre: Put the record back where you found it.
holocron.oldrepublic.echo.sith_thrane: Patience is a weapon. We have so much of it.
holocron.oldrepublic.echo.sith_torr: What was sealed should stay sealed.
holocron.oldrepublic.echo.sith_zarvos: Every victory leaves something on the field.
holocron.oldrepublic.echo.wayfarer_maeli: Every map is a promise that someone will come back.
holocron.oldrepublic.echo.wayfarer_pell: Still walking? Good. So am I, in a way.

journal.oldrepublic.codex.holocron_archi:
The codex Orren Vasch took from Lord Zarvos's inner vault, opened with a key the Watch should never have had.

Zarvos's teaching sits under Vasch's notes like a coal under ash: strike when the enemy is still whole, and their strength is yours to take.

Vasch says he took it so no one else would. His notes stop being careful halfway through.

Orren Vasch recorded this one for whoever came after him. No Order's seal, no gatekeeper's ceremony: just his voice, tired and very calm.

He says he took the Archive because a peace bought by surrender would have sold it next. He says a lot of things.

The last thing he says is about walking lightly. I think it is the only part he wrote for himself.

The Watch's own records, with Orren Vasch's annotations threaded through them: restorations, cross-references, small corrections in a patient hand.

The Council ordered half of the Archive destroyed after the Treaty, so the Empire could never read it. Vasch refused. Every note he left is a quiet argument that he was right.

Reading it, I can almost believe him.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.holocron_jedi_:
Knight Ruan Ketterin held the eastern pass for nineteen days with eleven Knights. Four came back.

Then came the Treaty of Coruscant, and the war was declared over by people a long way from here. The Empire's patrols kept coming for a season, and the Watch lost its Masters, its students and half its Archive in that peace.

He reads the names of the seven at the end. I wrote them down.

Master Aveth Morrane founded the Watch enclave on this frontier, long before the war. His holocron is calm and plain-spoken, like a teacher who has said the same thing a thousand times and still means it.

The Watch kept records because memory is a duty: every failure written down, so it is never repeated. A Jedi who forgets is only a warrior.

I understand Vasch a little better now. I am not sure I like that.

Ione Sarrow healed through the whole of the old war on this frontier. She does not talk about victories. She talks about the count: soldiers of both armies, settlers, children.

Her teaching is about breath, the part of healing that clears poison and weakness from the blood, the part that is closer to stubbornness than to kindness.

She sounds tired. She also sounds like she would do it all again.

Archivist Sela Vanterre taught Orren Vasch to read holocrons. She remembers him as patient and brilliant, the student she expected to keep the Archive long after her.

"He loved the Archive more than the people it was for." She says it without anger, which is worse.

Whatever he has become, he started here, putting records back on shelves with careful hands.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.holocron_sith_:
Overseer Calix Thrane recorded this briefing for Imperial Intelligence, and sealed it for good reason.

The Empire does not want this frontier for its soil. It wants the tombs, the kyber, and the old pilgrim roads that run around the Republic's back door. The Treaty only changed the timetable.

I wonder how many officers at the outpost have heard this. I wonder how many would care.

Ilvane Torr kept the seals on these tombs. They were not lost to time: the Sith sealed them on purpose, because some of what lies inside was too dangerous even for them.

The seals are broken now. Torr's holocron knows it, and it is angry in a way the others are not.

Someone came before me with patience and a key. I think I know his name.

Ysolde earned her name by refusing every master, rival and Emperor's envoy who tried to make her kneel. Strength, she says, is the only law that enforces itself.

Her teaching is cruel and practical: let the lightning cling, so the enemy is still slow when it ends.

She never says what became of her. I suspect she did not kneel then, either.

Lord Hadrek Zarvos built his tomb as a storehouse, not a grave. The Sith Lords of this frontier sealed their power in stone to wait for a worthy hand.

His lesson is hunger: every fallen enemy leaves strength behind for whoever is close enough to take it.

His inner vault was empty when I found the holocron. Someone had opened it before me, carefully, with a key.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.holocron_wayfa:
Maelis Dunn drew the frontier's maps for anyone who paid. Every one of them leaves out the same thing: a watchtower the Watch kept over the great sinkhole, struck from the charts at their request.

Whatever the Watch hid there, the tower is gone now, and the sinkhole took the rest. Maelis thought someone would go looking one day.

I have marked where she says it stood. I have not decided whether to go.

Osk Brevan surveyed this sector for the Republic before the war, alone, in a ship that could land on a gravel bar. Most of the old charts the armies use out here started as his.

His lesson was not about the Force at all, or not only. Move so the ground does not speak of you. Let the sleeping things go on sleeping.

The recording ends mid-sentence. I hope he finished the chart.

Pell never had a master and seems proud of it. The recording is cheerful, patient, and full of road dust: how to keep going when there is nobody to tell you that you are doing it right.

Practise, not teaching. Lift what blocks the way. Walk until the walking stops hurting, and then walk a little more.

I think Pell would have liked the people out here. Nobody taught them either.

Tessaly Arn belonged to no Order. She walked the pilgrim roads that once ran between the Watch enclave and the Sith tombs, when people still crossed this frontier to learn rather than to fight.

The roads are gone, but she says the Force keeps its own maps. Stillness first. Then the ground tells you where the old stones lie, where the hidden things wait, and which way the next holocron calls.

She asked nothing of me except that I keep walking.
